# Keep one report of everything that is broken

The pager sees a slice of what fires. The rest reaches a channel as one line per alert, and
some failures fire nothing at all. This skill runs a watcher that reads every active alert,
adds probes for the failures that no rule sees, and folds both into problems: one per subject
and component, one per alert name when it fires on many subjects together. The watcher keeps a
report of what is open, what changed this cycle, what is chronic and what resolved. It answers
"what is broken right now", "what changed since I last looked" and "is this new".

## Invariants

- Dedup by subject, not by alert. Every alert name on one subject and component is one
  problem. One alert name on many subjects that started together is one fleet problem, which
  usually has one cause (a dependency, a rollout, a provider). Read fleet problems first.
- A problem resolves only after it was absent for {{oncall.resolve_after}} cycles, and only if
  every source that reported it answered. An unreachable source is a `SOURCE-DOWN` event and
  freezes its problems; it never resolves them.
- The report is as fresh as its last cycle, and its header says when that was. A watcher on a
  laptop stops when the laptop sleeps; a report older than two cycles proves nothing.
- A quiet rule is not a healthy system. The probes cover failures that fire nothing; when a
  rule starts to cover the same failure, the probe goes.
- `{{oncall.loud}}` and above is loud. Below `{{oncall.floor}}` a problem is never marked new and
  never reaches the stream; the report and `events.log` still keep it.

## Quick path

Credentials are the token file or env var that `wikiloop.toml` names under
`[oncall.alertmanager]` and `[oncall.prometheus]`. Run from the plugin root, the directory
above `skills/`:

```
# one look: a cycle, the report on stdout
python3 {{core.path}}/oncall/watch.py --once

# keep watching: one stdout line per change, the report rewritten in place every cycle;
# --kube-context adds a restarted container's last error line (repeat it per cluster)
python3 {{core.path}}/oncall/watch.py --kube-context <cluster label>=<kube context>
```

State, report and event log live in `{{oncall_doc.state_dir}}` (`--state-dir` moves them). The
first cycle prints one `BASELINE` line instead of a line per open problem; after that only
`NEW`, `REOPENED`, `ESCALATED`, `SPREAD`, `RESOLVED`, `SOURCE-DOWN`, `SOURCE-UP` and a
`HEARTBEAT` every {{oncall_doc.heartbeat}}. Stdout skips problems below `{{oncall.floor}}`
(`--stream-min-severity` moves the floor) and a flapping problem's repeats
([checks.md](references/checks.md), Events and resolution); the report and `events.log` keep
everything.

In Claude Code, run the loop under Monitor with the longest timeout and re-arm it on expiry.
`/{{oncall.command}}` does this for you when no watch runs here: no cycle in the last
{{oncall_doc.off_after}}, or a last cycle older than two cycles. It asks the model to start the
watch once; a second `/{{oncall.command}}` before the first cycle does not start a second
watcher.

While a watch runs, the plugin shows its state without a setting (`hooks/oncall/`). The line
under the prompt shows the counts and the loud problems, cut to the width of the terminal. A
pane with the report's sections opens once in each session; a click on the line or
`/{{oncall.command}}` opens it again, or closes it while it is shown. `/{{oncall.command}} off`
hides the line and the pane until the next `/{{oncall.command}}`, and asks the model to stop the
watch. Under each problem the pane links the alert's web view and the channel it reaches. Both
read only the local state and show nothing when no cycle ran for {{oncall_doc.off_after}}. They
warn when the last cycle is older than two cycles of the interval.

When you tell a person what broke, use the report's sections in their order, as short bullets,
not as a wide table: **New and changed**, {{oncall_doc.sections_list}}, **Other open
problems**. Give chronic problems one or two lines in total. In a section, higher tiers come
first, and fleet problems before the subjects they cover. For each problem, open the skill for
its subject before you guess at a cause.
